image_description: A close-up, eye-level shot of a grey whale's head and upper torso emerging vertically from choppy, teal-green ocean water. The whale's skin is dark grey to black with distinctive white mottling and barnacle clusters, particularly on the rostrum. The background shows a distant, hazy shoreline under a pale sky.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle of the photo (frontal/slightly low) and the emergence from water obscure the top of the head where the blowholes are located. They are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image clearly displays the characteristic mottled pattern with white callosities and barnacle clusters on the dark grey skin of the rostrum and head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only captures the head and anterior body. The posterior back where dorsal knuckles would be is submerged or out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck/shoulder region are visible. The full spindle shape cannot be verified due to cropping and submersion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible skin texture and coloration match the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed or submerged; baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located further back on the body and are completely submerged/out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is entirely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: High-resolution details on the snout show the rough, bumpy texture typical of grey whale callosities.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Slight softness/blurring at the exact contact line between the whale's skin and the water surface. While some blur is expected due to motion/water refraction, the edge lacks the crisp displacement one might expect from a heavy object breaking the surface tension, suggesting minor generative smoothing.
The horizon line is slightly uneven and the distant landmass has a 'painted' or overly smooth quality compared to the detailed foreground, typical of AI depth handling, but not structurally failing.
